items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: Sam Wooding sent for me -- he was organizing a band... with Sam Wooding's band... I went into Sam Wooding's band

ctx.x: Is that right? Was Duke, when he first came out, after Sonny Greer made the switch for him, and came out as Duke Ellington's Band, was the name of it -- overnight it was Duke Ellington's Band, right?

Yeah, yeah. How he got in the Cotton Club, see, I had been on tour with Wooding -- which we will talk about later on, and came back and we had been offered the job at the Cotton Club, and they offered us $1,100.00 a week which was a big salary then. And we said, 'No, we started in

Harlem, we're not coming back to Harlem. We've been to Russia we've played all over the world, we played for the kings and queens of the world, we're going to come back to Harlem?" Duke had his band together and organized and he took the job. He had a 10-piece band then, and he took the job. And the rest is history. That's how he got in the Cotton Club. I refused. I told Sam (unintelligible) "What should I do?" He said, "No, no, don't go back to Harlem." It was my decision not to go back to Harlem. After what…

items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: like Garvin Bushell and the other Saxophone player and Bobby and them would be glad to get that -- go off.

ctx.x: No, that's what you miss. You miss that experience. Now when we were in the Nest, way back in the days of the Nest, Henry Bussey, Frank Forani, Johnny Dunn, Tommy Morris, these are fellows all used to come up. Bechet, Sidney Bechet, all of them used to come up and sit with band and play a time.
